Carboxin (75% WP) is used against Rhizoctonia Root Rot (Rhizoctonia solani). FRAC Group 7, mode of action: SDHI (Mitochondrial complex II) (Systemic (Seed/Root treatment)). Critical crop stage: Pre-planting (rootstock treatment). Spray timing: Dip roots or drench soil; protects young roots. Rainfastness: N/A hrs. PHI: N/A days, REI: 12 hrs. Resistance risk: Medium. Rotate with FRAC groups: Biologicals (Trichoderma). Pollinator safety: Safe. Beneficial impact: Low.

Carbendazim (50% WP) is used against Fusarium Root Rot (Fusarium spp.). FRAC Group 1, mode of action: MBC (Mitosis inhibitor) (Systemic (Soil drench)). Critical crop stage: Pre-planting or early post-plant. Spray timing: Soil drench; resistance risk; limited efficacy. Rainfastness: N/A hrs. PHI: 30+ days, REI: 12 hrs. Resistance risk: High. Rotate with FRAC groups: Biologicals, Soil solarization. Pollinator safety: Safe. Beneficial impact: Moderate.

Copper Hydroxide (77% WP) is used against Crown Gall (Agrobacterium vitis). FRAC Group M1, mode of action: Multi-site (Bactericide) (Protective (Wound sealant)). Critical crop stage: Dormant (post-pruning). Spray timing: Apply to pruning wounds; biological K84 is superior. Rainfastness: N/A hrs. PHI: 1–14 days, REI: 24 hrs. Resistance risk: Low-Medium. Rotate with FRAC groups: A. radiobacter K84 (biological). Pollinator safety: Safe. Beneficial impact: Moderate.

topic: Streptomycin + Tetracycline (9%+1%) (Crown Gall / Bacterial Leaf Spot)
content: Streptomycin + Tetracycline (9%+1%) is used against Crown Gall / Bacterial Leaf Spot (Agrobacterium / Xanthomonas). FRAC Group UNK (Antibiotic), mode of action: Protein synthesis inhibitors (Systemic (Bactericide)). Critical crop stage: Early season. Spray timing: For severe bacterial outbreaks; resistance risk; limited use. Rainfastness: 1–2 hrs. PHI: 14–21 days, REI: 12 hrs. Resistance risk: High. Rotate with FRAC groups: Copper (M1). Pollinator safety: Safe. Beneficial impact: High (affects microbiome).

Copper Hydroxide (77% WP) is used against Bacterial Leaf Spot (Xanthomonas spp.). FRAC Group M1, mode of action: Multi-site (Bactericide) (Protective Contact). Critical crop stage: Early season; before rain events. Spray timing: Apply protectively; copper resistance reported. Rainfastness: 1–2 hrs. PHI: 1–14 days, REI: 24 hrs. Resistance risk: Low-Medium. Rotate with FRAC groups: Streptomycin, Biologicals. Pollinator safety: Safe. Beneficial impact: Moderate.

Imidacloprid (IRAC 4A) is used against Vector for Pierce's Disease (Xylella fastidiosa - leafhoppers). FRAC Group 4A (Insecticide), mode of action: Nicotinic receptor agonist (Systemic (Vector control)). Critical crop stage: Throughout growing season. Spray timing: Target leafhopper vectors; reduce spread. Rainfastness: 2–4 hrs. PHI: 7–14 days, REI: 12 hrs. Resistance risk: High (neonic). Rotate with FRAC groups: 4C, 9C, 3A. Pollinator safety: High Toxicity. Beneficial impact: High Impact.

Spirotetramat (IRAC 23) is used against Vector for Leafroll / Red Blotch (Mealybugs). FRAC Group 23 (Insecticide), mode of action: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibitor (Systemic (Vector control)). Critical crop stage: Early season (crawler emergence). Spray timing: Suppress mealybug populations; reduce virus spread. Rainfastness: 2–4 hrs. PHI: 7 days, REI: 12 hrs. Resistance risk: Low. Rotate with FRAC groups: 16, 7C, 4C. Pollinator safety: Moderate. Beneficial impact: Moderate.

Buprofezin (IRAC 16) is used against Vector for Leafroll (Mealybugs / Scales). FRAC Group 16 (Insecticide), mode of action: Chitin synthesis inhibitor (Contact (Vector control)). Critical crop stage: Crawler emergence. Spray timing: Suppress vector populations; IGR safe to adults. Rainfastness: 2–4 hrs. PHI: 7–14 days, REI: 12 hrs. Resistance risk: Low. Rotate with FRAC groups: 23, 7C, 4C. Pollinator safety: Moderate. Beneficial impact: Low.

Fluopyram (34.48% SC) is used against Vector for Fanleaf (Nematode - Xiphinema index). FRAC Group 7 (Nematicide), mode of action: SDHI (Soil drench (Nematicide)). Critical crop stage: Pre-planting or early root flush. Spray timing: Reduce nematode vector populations; prevents virus transmission. Rainfastness: N/A hrs. PHI: 30+ days, REI: 12 hrs. Resistance risk: Low. Rotate with FRAC groups: Fluensulfone, Cyclobutrifluoram. Pollinator safety: Safe. Beneficial impact: Moderate.

Fluensulfone (2% GR) is used against Vector for Fanleaf (Nematode - Xiphinema index). FRAC Group UNK (Nematicide), mode of action: Nematicide (fumigant-like) (Soil incorporation). Critical crop stage: Pre-planting. Spray timing: Reduce nematode populations; prevents GFLV spread. Rainfastness: N/A hrs. PHI: 30 days, REI: 48 hrs. Resistance risk: Low. Rotate with FRAC groups: Fluopyram. Pollinator safety: Safe. Beneficial impact: Moderate.

topic: No Direct Chemical (Grapevine Fanleaf / Leafroll / Red Blotch / Bois Noir / Flavescence Dorée)
content: No Direct Chemical is used against Grapevine Fanleaf / Leafroll / Red Blotch / Bois Noir / Flavescence Dorée (Viruses & Phytoplasmas). FRAC Group N/A, mode of action: N/A (N/A). Critical crop stage: N/A. Spray timing: No curative chemicals exist. Management relies on: (1) Virus-tested planting material (most critical), (2) Vector control (insecticides/nematicides listed above), (3) Rogueing (remove infected vines immediately), (4) Sanitation (remove infected plant debris). Rainfastness: N/A hrs. PHI: N/A days, REI: N/A hrs. Resistance risk: N/A. Rotate with FRAC groups: N/A. Pollinator safety: N/A. Beneficial impact: N/A.

No Direct Chemical is used against Sooty Mold (Capnodium spp.). FRAC Group N/A, mode of action: N/A (N/A). Critical crop stage: N/A. Spray timing: Control underlying honeydew-producing insects (Mealybugs, Aphids, Whiteflies, Scale). Use IRAC 23, 16, 7C, 4A/4C. Wash off sooty mold with high-pressure water post-insect control.. Rainfastness: N/A hrs. PHI: Follow insecticide days, REI: Follow insecticide hrs. Resistance risk: N/A. Rotate with FRAC groups: N/A. Pollinator safety: Follow insecticide. Beneficial impact: Follow insecticide.

Downy Mildew: Rotate M3 → 4 → 40 → 27 → 11 (limit 11 to 2x/season). Powdery Mildew: Rotate M2 → 3 → 11 → 50 (limit 3 & 11 to 2x/season). Botrytis: Rotate M4/M3 → 2 → 12 → 17 (limit high-risk FRAC 2/12 to 2x/season).
Mancozeb (66 days) dictates final spray timing. For near-harvest, use Captan (3–7d), Sulphur (7–14d), or Biopesticides. Always calculate backwards from harvest.
For Trunk Diseases (Esca, Eutypa, Dead Arm, Crown Gall), apply Copper-based or biological (K84/Trichoderma) wound protectants within 24 hours of pruning—this is the single most effective prevention.

NO CHEMICAL CURES exist. Management is 100% dependent on: (1) Certified virus-free planting material, (2) Vector suppression (insecticides for leafhoppers/mealybugs; nematicides for nematodes), (3) Immediate rogueing of symptomatic vines.

Downy Mildew: Apply protectants (M3/M1) before rain; apply penetrants (4, 40, 27) within 72h post-infection. Powdery Mildew: Apply protectants (M2) before infection (no free water needed); apply DMIs (3) curatively. Botrytis: Apply at bloom and veraison—prevent latent infections.
Ensure complete canopy coverage—diseases like Downy Mildew require underside leaf coverage; Powdery Mildew requires even distribution. Use 1000–1500 L/ha water volume with proper nozzles.
Document: Date, AI, FRAC group, Crop stage, Weather (temp/RH/rain), Disease severity, PHI/REI compliance. Essential for resistance management and export MRL compliance.

>35–40°C; leaf scorch, berry sunburn, poor fruit set, stomatal closure Critical crop stage: Flowering, Berry set, Veraison. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Salicylic Acid, S-ABA, Ascophyllum nodosum, Glycine Betaine, Kaolin (physical). Application timing: 2–3 days before forecast heat; repeat 7 days later if heat persists. Key management practices: Early morning spray; increase irrigation; provide 30% shade net if possible; apply K-silicate to thicken cuticle. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Avoid mixing with spray oils or EC formulations during heat (phytotoxicity). Compatible with most contact fungicides (Captan) if done at dusk.

Low temperatures (0–10°C); slow growth, tissue injury, chlorosis Critical crop stage: Early spring (bud swell to shoot growth). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed extract (Ecklonia), Proline, Salicylic Acid, Brassinolide. Application timing: 24–48 hours before cold spell; repeat after cold front passes. Key management practices: Avoid pruning before cold event; apply anti-transpirant; ensure soil is moist (wet soil retains heat). Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Do not mix with copper if temperature <10°C (phytotoxicity). Compatible with mancozeb (M3).

Freezing temps; death of buds, shoots, flowers Critical crop stage: Bud break, Green tip, Early shoot. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed (Ascophyllum), Salicylic Acid, Proline, Glycine Betaine. Application timing: 24–48 hours before forecast frost. Key management practices: Overhead irrigation during frost (if safe); avoid spraying if already frozen (ice crystals worsen damage). Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Hold all oil-based products. Compatible with copper only if applied 5–7 days apart (not together).

0–10°C non-freezing; delayed growth, chlorosis, poor pollen development Critical crop stage: Dormancy break to flowering. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Brassinolide, Seaweed, Amino acids (Arginine/Glutamic). Application timing: At bud swell and again at 2-leaf stage. Key management practices: Maintain good potassium nutrition; use floating row covers for young vines. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Compatible with Pyrethroids (IRAC 3A) and Neonicotinoids (4A) when mixed.

Direct intense sunlight; brown/black patches, corky skin, shrivelled berries Critical crop stage: Post-veraison (berry ripening). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: S-ABA, Calcium (CaCl₂ or Ca-amino chelate), Seaweed, Kaolin. Application timing: 2–3 weeks before veraison; repeat at 50% colour change. Key management practices: Leaf-positioning to shade clusters; apply ABA to enhance natural antioxidant production. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: ABA degrades in alkaline pH (>7.0). Do not mix with sulfur (heat stress + sulfur = burn).

Excess UV; leaf bronzing, reduced photosynthesis, berry skin damage Critical crop stage: Throughout canopy development (especially post-veraison). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Ascorbic Acid (Vit C), Salicylic Acid, Melatonin. Application timing: Weekly during high UV periods (summer). Key management practices: Use UV-reflective kaolin; maintain dense canopy. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Compatible with mancozeb and captan; avoid mixing with oxidising agents (chlorine).

Strong winds; leaf tearing, shoot breakage, flower drop, desiccation Critical crop stage: Bloom, Early shoot growth, Pre-harvest. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed, Potassium Silicate, Brassinolide, Proline. Application timing: Immediately after storm event; repeat at 7 days. Key management practices: Install windbreaks (trees/netting); hold irrigation pre-wind to reduce desiccation. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Brassinolide compatible with most fungicides except high-pH copper.

Physical injury; shredded leaves, broken shoots, berry scars, open wounds Critical crop stage: Throughout canopy (spring–summer). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed, Amino acids (Glycine/Proline), Brassinolide, Chitosan (wound healing). Application timing: Within 24–48 hours after hail event. Key management practices: Prune broken shoots; apply protective fungicide first (to prevent rot), wait 2–3 days then apply biostimulant. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Hold copper (M1) for 5 days after severe wounding (risk of burn). Compatible with Captan and Mancozeb after the initial protective spray.

Sudden vine death, scorched bark, unexplained wilting Critical crop stage: Any stage (summer storms). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed, Humic Acid (soil drench), Amino acids. Application timing: Immediately after event, if vine is salvageable. Key management practices: Remove dead parts; improve root aeration; no chemical cure – only recovery support. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Not applicable; focus on soil health rather than tank mixing.

Irregular weather; altered flowering, fruit set, berry composition Critical crop stage: Flowering, Veraison. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: GA₃ (for set), S-ABA (for ripening), Seaweed (general resilience). Application timing: Adjust PGR timing based on actual phenology, not calendar. Key management practices: Monitor phenological models; adjust pruning and irrigation schedules. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Standard PGR precautions apply.

Fire smoke; reduced photosynthesis, off-flavours (smoke taint), necrosis Critical crop stage: Post-veraison (berry quality). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Salicylic Acid, Ascorbic Acid, Seaweed, Melatonin. Application timing: Immediately after smoke exposure; repeat 7 days later. Key management practices: Delay harvest if possible; test for smoke taint; use anti-oxidant foliar sprays. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Compatible with contact fungicides (Captan). Avoid mixing with oxidising agents.

Leaf spotting, chlorosis, reduced growth, premature senescence Critical crop stage: Throughout season (summer). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Salicylic Acid, Ascorbic Acid, Seaweed. Application timing: At first symptom; repeat every 10–14 days. Key management practices: Improve canopy ventilation; avoid planting near industrial zones. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Compatible with most insecticides; hold copper if symptoms severe.

Industrial/road dust; reduced photosynthesis, clogged stomata Critical crop stage: Spring–Summer. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed, Potassium Silicate. Application timing: After dust storms; wash foliage with clean water first. Key management practices: Install windbreaks; use overhead irrigation to wash dust. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Wash dust off before spraying (otherwise dust absorbs the spray).

Water deficit; wilting, reduced berry size, leaf drop, poor sugar accumulation Critical crop stage: Berry enlargement, Veraison. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Humic Acid, Fulvic Acid, Seaweed, S-ABA, Potassium Silicate, Glycine Betaine. Application timing: Soil application at root flush; foliar during dry spells. Key management practices: Apply ABA to close stomata; use drip irrigation; mulch to conserve moisture. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: ABA incompatible with sulfur (adds stress). Humic acid compatible with most insecticides (except copper).

Excess moisture; root suffocation, yellowing, wilting, vine decline Critical crop stage: Monsoon, heavy rains (early season). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Amino acids (Arginine/Glutamic), Seaweed, Trichoderma harzianum (soil drench). Application timing: Immediately after water recedes. Key management practices: Improve drainage; raise beds; avoid cultivation when wet. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Trichoderma is completely incompatible with chemical fungicides – maintain 7–10 day gap.

Prolonged submersion; root rot, oxygen deficiency, vine death Critical crop stage: Post-cyclone / extreme rain. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed, Fulvic Acid, Trichoderma, Arbuscular Mycorrhizae (AMF). Application timing: As soon as water subsides; soil drench with mycorrhizae after soil dries. Key management practices: Assess root damage; prune canopy to balance root loss. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Do not apply chemical fungicides to soil for 2 weeks post-flood (they worsen root stress).

High soluble salts (NaCl, CaCl₂); leaf burn, marginal necrosis, stunted growth, poor yield Critical crop stage: Early growth, Flowering. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Humic Acid, Calcium (Ca²⁺ nutrient), Glycine Betaine, Seaweed, Potassium Silicate. Application timing: Soil application pre-plant / early season; foliar when symptoms appear. Key management practices: Leach salts with excess irrigation; use gypsum (CaSO₄) to replace Na; apply humic to chelate salts. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Humic acid compatible with phosphorus fertilisers. Do not mix with strongly acidic products (pH <5).

High sodium (Na⁺); poor soil structure, nutrient imbalance (Ca/Mg displacement), poor root function Critical crop stage: Early vegetative growth. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Gypsum (CaSO₄) (soil), Humic Acid, Calcium foliar. Application timing: Soil application at pre-planting or early season. Key management practices: Apply gypsum to flocculate soil; improve organic matter; avoid sodium-containing fertilisers. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Compatible with most non-ionic products; avoid mixing with high-phosphate fertilisers (precipitation).

>7.5; iron/zinc/manganese deficiency (lime-induced chlorosis) Critical crop stage: Throughout season (chlorosis appears on young leaves). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Fe-EDDHA, Fulvic Acid, Sulfur (soil acidifier), Seaweed, Citric Acid (acidifier). Application timing: Fe-EDDHA soil drench at bud break; foliar Fe + fulvic when symptoms show. Key management practices: Acidify irrigation water to pH 6.0–6.5; apply elemental sulfur to soil in winter. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Never mix Fe-chelates with alkaline pesticides (e.g., Bordeaux mixture). Fulvic acid enhances Fe uptake – compatible with mancozeb.

<5.5; aluminium/manganese toxicity, nutrient imbalance (Ca/Mg deficiency) Critical crop stage: Root flush, Early growth. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Calcium (lime), Magnesium, Humic Acid (to buffer), AMF (to protect roots). Application timing: Apply lime (CaCO₃) 3–6 months before planting; humic acid at root flush. Key management practices: Raise pH with dolomitic lime; avoid acid-forming fertilisers (ammonium sulfate). Tank-mix/compatibility notes: AMF incompatible with fumigants and high-rate fungicides (maintain gap).

Pale green leaves, stunted growth, poor vigour, yellowing of older leaves Critical crop stage: Early vegetative growth, Post-harvest. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Protein Hydrolysates, Amino acids (glutamic acid), Azotobacter (bio-fixer), Seaweed. Application timing: At bud break, post-harvest, and during rapid growth. Key management practices: Apply balanced N (not excessive – causes excessive vegetative growth & botrytis); use slow-release forms. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Compatible with most insecticides (4A, 3A) and mancozeb. Do not mix with copper in high concentration (N + Cu can burn).

Purplish leaves, poor root development, delayed flowering, poor fruit set Critical crop stage: Pre-bloom, Root flush (early season). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Phosphite (PGR), Humic Acid (P-solubiliser), AMF (P-uptake), Bacillus megaterium (P-solubiliser). Application timing: Soil application at pre-planting / root flush; foliar at pre-bloom. Key management practices: Use AMF to increase P uptake; apply P in bands near roots; avoid P fixation with lime. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: AMF & Bacillus are incompatible with fumigants and high-rate fungicides – maintain 10-day gap. Humic acid compatible with P fertilisers.

Marginal leaf scorch, poor berry size/colour/sugar, weak shoots, brittle canes Critical crop stage: Veraison, Berry enlargement. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Potassium Silicate, K-Humate, Seaweed, S-ABA (improves K-mobilisation). Application timing: Soil application early; foliar K-silicate at veraison. Key management practices: K is mobile – apply via drip fertigation; avoid excess Mg (competes with K). Tank-mix/compatibility notes: K-silicate is compatible with most fungicides (except copper – forms insoluble copper silicate).

Poor berry firmness, berry cracking, tip dieback, weak cell walls Critical crop stage: Fruit set, Berry enlargement, Pre-harvest. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Calcium (CaCl₂, Ca-amino chelate), Amino acids (chelators), Fulvic Acid. Application timing: Foliar at pea-size and veraison; repeat every 10–14 days. Key management practices: Calcium is immobile – must target developing berries directly; avoid nitrate-N which competes with Ca uptake. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Calcium products are incompatible with sulfates (precipitation). Do not mix with sulfur in the same tank.

Interveinal chlorosis on older leaves (green veins, yellow interveinal areas) Critical crop stage: Post-bloom to veraison. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: MgSO₄ (Epsom salt), Seaweed, Amino acids. Application timing: Foliar MgSO₄ at 2% at post-bloom; soil application pre-season. Key management practices: Avoid high K fertilisers (K competes with Mg); apply dolomitic lime if pH low. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: MgSO₄ compatible with most fungicides; do not mix with calcium products in the same tank (precipitates gypsum).

Uniform yellowing of young leaves (similar to N, but starts on young leaves) Critical crop stage: Early vegetative growth. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Sulfur (elemental), Seaweed (contains S), Sulfate fertilisers. Application timing: Soil application in winter; foliar sulfate at early growth. Key management practices: Check pH – sulfur deficiency often linked to low OM soils; apply gypsum. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Elemental sulfur used as fungicide also corrects deficiency – avoid over-application (phytotoxicity).

Interveinal chlorosis on young leaves (yellow with green veins) Critical crop stage: Post-bud break, Early shoot growth. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Fe-EDDHA, Fe-EDTA, Fulvic Acid, Citric Acid (acidifier). Application timing: Soil drench at bud break; foliar Fe + fulvic when symptoms appear. Key management practices: Acidify irrigation to pH 6.0; avoid phosphate fertilisers near Fe (fixes Fe). Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Fe-chelates are incompatible with alkaline pesticides (Bordeaux, lime sulfur). Fulvic acid enhances Fe uptake – compatible with mancozeb.

Small leaves, shortened internodes ("little leaf"), rosetting, poor fruit set Critical crop stage: Pre-bloom (critical), Post-harvest. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: ZnSO₄ + Urea, Zn-EDTA, Amino acids (Zn-chelated), Humic Acid. Application timing: Foliar at pre-bloom (most effective) and post-harvest. Key management practices: Zn is immobile – need direct foliar targeting; add urea (0.5%) to improve penetration. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Never mix Zn with phosphorus (precipitates zinc phosphate). Compatible with most fungicides (except copper – reduces Zn uptake).

Interveinal chlorosis with speckling (young leaves), reduced growth, poor fruit set Critical crop stage: Early shoot growth, Pre-bloom. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: MnSO₄, Mn-EDTA, Seaweed (natural Mn), Citric acid (acidifier). Application timing: Foliar at early shoot growth (2–4 leaf stage). Key management practices: Mn deficiency common on high-pH soils; acidify irrigation; avoid excess Fe (competes). Tank-mix/compatibility notes: MnSO₄ compatible with most fungicides except high-pH products (Bordeaux, lime sulfur).

Poor fruit set, "hen and chick" (berry abortion), deformed berries, cracked berries, short shoots Critical crop stage: Pre-bloom (50% capfall) and early berry set. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Borax (Na₂B₄O₇), Boric acid, Sorbitol-complexed B. Application timing: Critical – 1 week before flowering and immediately after fruit set (pea size). Key management practices: Boron is immobile and toxic if overdose (precise measurement critical). Soil test before application.. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Compatible with most fungicides (captan, mancozeb). Avoid mixing with oils (causes droplet burn). Maintain pH 5.5–7.0 in tank.

Dieback of young shoots, poor leaf expansion, wilting of growing tips Critical crop stage: Early shoot growth. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: CuSO₄, Cu-EDTA, Seaweed. Application timing: Foliar at early shoot growth. Key management practices: Copper deficiency rare; usually corrected by fungicidal copper sprays – avoid overdose (toxicity). Tank-mix/compatibility notes: If using Cu for deficiency, do not mix with sulfur (phytotoxicity).

Poor nitrogen utilisation, chlorosis (similar to N deficiency), leaf margin necrosis Critical crop stage: Early growth. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Ammonium Molybdate, Mo-EDTA. Application timing: Foliar or seed-treatment. Key management practices: Mo is crucial for nitrate reductase; apply at low rates (gm/ha).. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Compatible with most products; avoid strong acids (pH <5).

Excess B; marginal leaf scorch, yellowing, premature leaf drop, root tip necrosis Critical crop stage: Any stage (due to over-application). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Gypsum (CaSO₄ – leach B), Irrigation (leaching), Humic acid (complexes excess B). Application timing: Immediately upon symptom recognition. Key management practices: Stop B application; leach soil with excess water; apply gypsum to precipitate B. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Gypsum compatible with most non-biological products.

Excess Cl in soil/water; leaf margin burn, premature senescence, reduced vigour Critical crop stage: Mid-season (hot & dry). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Leaching (excess irrigation), Gypsum, Seaweed (improves osmoregulation). Application timing: As soon as symptoms appear. Key management practices: Avoid chloride-based fertilisers (KCl, NH₄Cl); use sulfate forms (K₂SO₄). Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Gypsum compatible with most products.

High Na; leaf burn, reduced water uptake, poor root function Critical crop stage: Throughout season. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Gypsum, Humic Acid, Calcium (foliar), Leaching. Application timing: Pre-planting (soil) and as symptoms appear. Key management practices: Replace Na with Ca on exchange sites; apply gypsum; improve drainage. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Humic acid compatible with most, but do not mix with strong acids.

Low pH soils; excess Mn; leaf crinkling, brown speckling, stunted roots Critical crop stage: Early growth. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Lime (CaCO₃ – raise pH), Organic matter (bind Mn), Seaweed. Application timing: Apply lime 3–6 months before planting. Key management practices: Raise soil pH >5.5; avoid acidifying fertilisers. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Not relevant for foliar mixing – focus on soil remediation.

Excessive Cu sprays; stunted roots, leaf bronzing, iron chlorosis (Cu-Fe antagonism) Critical crop stage: Post-spray (following repeated Cu applications). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Organic matter (bind Cu), Iron (foliar Fe-EDDHA to correct chlorosis), Seaweed. Application timing: Stop Cu sprays; apply organic compost; foliar Fe to correct symptoms. Key management practices: Hold all copper-based fungicides for at least 1 season.. Tank-mix/compatibility notes:

Excessive vegetative growth, soft tissues, delayed maturity, increased disease (botrytis), poor colour Critical crop stage: Post-veraison (if over-applied). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Paclobutrazol (growth retardant), Potassium (balance N), Seaweed. Application timing: Reduce N applications; apply K to balance; Paclobutrazol only in extreme cases. Key management practices: Paclobutrazol is strong – do not mix with GA₃ (opposite effects).. Tank-mix/compatibility notes:

Excess K (over-application); Mg & Ca deficiency symptoms, poor berry firmness Critical crop stage: Pre-harvest. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Gypsum (Ca to balance), Seaweed. Application timing: Stop K applications; apply Ca (foliar) to correct. Key management practices: Gypsum compatible with most non-biological products.. Tank-mix/compatibility notes:

Off-target exposure; leaf cupping, strapping, necrosis, stem cracking, berry drop Critical crop stage: Throughout season (most severe at early growth). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed extract, Humic Acid, Brassinolide, Amino acids (Proline), Activated charcoal (soil). Application timing: Immediately (within 24–48 hours) after suspected exposure. Key management practices: Hold all new pesticide sprays for 5–7 days to avoid further stress; use charcoal soil drench to bind root-uptake herbicides. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Do not mix with additional pesticides during recovery phase. Brassinolide is compatible with contact fungicides (Captan) if needed.

Leaf necrosis, curling, marginal burn, browning due to tank-mix errors or high rates Critical crop stage: Post-application. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed, Amino acids, Brassinolide, Humic acid (foliar). Application timing: Immediately after phytotoxicity is noted. Key management practices: Flush leaves with clean water (if recent); identify the cause (pH, rate, incompatibility); adjust future mixes. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Hold all further chemical applications for 7 days; use only water + biostimulants.

Leaf burn, phytotoxicity from oil + sulfur or oil + high temp Critical crop stage: Post-spray (hot weather). Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Seaweed, Amino acids, Fulvic acid. Application timing: Immediately after symptom appearance. Key management practices: Reduce oil rates in future; never apply oils with sulfur >30°C. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Oil-based products are incompatible with most PGRs (GA3, ABA) and sulfur.

Heavy machinery; poor root growth, restricted aeration, waterlogging, poor nutrient uptake Critical crop stage: Root flush, Early season. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Humic Acid, AMF (improves structure), Gypsum (breaks compaction), Seaweed. Application timing: Soil application pre-planting or during root flush (at drip-line). Key management practices: Sub-soil if possible; avoid heavy machinery when wet; add organic matter (compost). Tank-mix/compatibility notes: AMF incompatible with fumigants and high-rate fungicides – maintain 10-day gap.

Poor soil aeration; root suffocation, wilting, yellowing, decay (anaerobic conditions) Critical crop stage: Monsoon, heavy compaction. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Hydrogen Peroxide (low dose – 0.1% for oxygenation), Humic Acid, Trichoderma. Application timing: Immediately after waterlogging; drench soil. Key management practices: Improve drainage; add organic matter; avoid over-irrigation. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Hydrogen peroxide is incompatible with living microbes (kills them). Humic acid compatible with most except copper.

Poor irrigation water (high bicarbonates, salinity, EC); salt accumulation, nutrient lock-up Critical crop stage: Throughout season. Recommended biostimulant/PGR: Humic Acid (chelates salts), Gypsum (corrects bicarbonates), Fulvic Acid. Application timing: At each irrigation (if possible) – acidify water first (e.g., citric acid). Key management practices: Test water quality (EC, SAR, bicarbonates); acidify to pH 6.0–6.5; use drip irrigation. Tank-mix/compatibility notes: Humic acid is compatible with most, but if using phosphorus fertilisers, apply humic first to prevent precipitation.

Category: Auxins. Major use in grapes: Root initiation in cuttings, early cell elongation. Critical phenological stage: Cutting propagation, early root flush. Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–500 ppm. Application method: Dip / Foliar (rare in field). Precautions: Unstable in light – use fresh; rarely used commercially in field grapes.

Category: Auxins. Major use in grapes: Rooting of cuttings (nursery), promotion of root mass. Critical phenological stage: Cutting propagation (pre-planting). Recommended dose (conceptual): 1000–3000 ppm (dip). Application method: Quick-dip / Base-dip. Precautions: Store in dark; use alcohol to dissolve first; do not exceed 5000 ppm (phytotoxicity).

Category: Auxins. Major use in grapes: Fruit thinning, preventing berry drop (abscission control), rooting. Critical phenological stage: Early post-bloom (thinning), Pre-harvest (drop control), Cutting propagation. Recommended dose (conceptual): 10–50 ppm (foliar); 2000–4000 ppm (root dip). Application method: Foliar / Dip. Precautions: Sensitive to hard water – use conditioner. Overdose causes fruit cracking. Do not mix with oils.

Category: Auxins. Major use in grapes: Fruit set promotion (very low doses), parthenocarpy. Critical phenological stage: Early flowering (spray at 80–100% bloom). Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.5–1 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Extremely phytotoxic if dose >2 ppm. Do NOT mix with any other product. Use only where label specifically allows.

Category: Gibberellins. Major use in grapes: Berry elongation, bunch loosening, berry sizing, seedlessness stimulation. Critical phenological stage: 1. Pre-bloom (loosening: 10–20 ppm) 2. 7–10 days post-bloom (sizing: 20–50 ppm). Recommended dose (conceptual): 10–50 ppm (varies by variety). Application method: Foliar / Cluster dip. Precautions: Degrades in alkaline pH (>7) – acidify water to 5.5–6.5. Add non-ionic surfactant. Do not mix with copper or alkaline products.

Category: Gibberellins. Major use in grapes: Berry enlargement, similar to GA₃ but more active on some varieties. Critical phenological stage: Post-bloom (berry cell division). Recommended dose (conceptual): 10–30 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: GA₄ is more thermally stable than GA₃; same pH precautions apply.

Category: Gibberellins. Major use in grapes: Mixture for cell division & elongation; used in some commercial blends. Critical phenological stage: Post-bloom to early berry development. Recommended dose (conceptual): 20–40 ppm (combined). Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Same as GA₃ – check label for exact ratio; generally less heat-sensitive than pure GA₃.

Category: Cytokinins. Major use in grapes: Cell division, berry development, improved fruit set, reducing "hens and chicks". Critical phenological stage: Early berry development (3–5 mm berry size). Recommended dose (conceptual): 25–50 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Avoid >35°C (causes leaf necrosis). Works synergistically with GA₃ (often combined). Do not mix with alkaline products.

Category: Cytokinins. Major use in grapes: Cell division, delayed senescence (generally replaced by 6-BA in grapes). Critical phenological stage: Early berry set. Recommended dose (conceptual): 10–25 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Rarely used – less effective than 6-BA in grapes.

Category: Cytokinins. Major use in grapes: Cell division, stress recovery (more expensive). Critical phenological stage: Post-stress, early berry development. Recommended dose (conceptual): 5–20 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Natural origin – sensitive to heat; store at 4°C.

Category: Cytokinins. Major use in grapes: Potent cytokinin – used for shoot regeneration (lab) & berry set (limited field use). Critical phenological stage: Berry set (experimental). Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.5–2 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Overdose causes severe leaf cupping. Use extreme caution.

Category: Cytokinins. Major use in grapes: Berry enlargement, improved fruit set (very potent). Critical phenological stage: Berry set (pea-size stage, 10–14 days after bloom). Recommended dose (conceptual): 2–5 ppm. Application method: Foliar / Cluster dip. Precautions: Very potent – overdose causes hard, cracked berries or "bottle-neck" stems. Do not mix with oils.

Category: Ethylene Regulators. Major use in grapes: Uniform ripening, colour development, cluster loosening (reduced compactness). Critical phenological stage: Pre-harvest (2–3 weeks before harvest) or Veraison. Recommended dose (conceptual): 200–500 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Do NOT mix with alkaline products (releases ethylene prematurely). Do not apply if rain expected within 6 hours.

Category: Ethylene Regulators. Major use in grapes: Precursor to ethylene – used in research; not common in commercial practice. Critical phenological stage: Not standard in field grapes. Recommended dose (conceptual): –. Application method: –. Precautions: Limited commercial use.

Category: Growth Retardants. Major use in grapes: Vegetative growth regulation (reduces shoot vigour) – use selectively. Critical phenological stage: Post-harvest or early spring (soil application). Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.5–2 g a.i./vine (soil). Application method: Soil drench / Foliar. Precautions: Strong permanent effect – do not apply to young vines. It can delay ripening. Do NOT mix with GA₃ (opposite effect).

Category: Growth Retardants. Major use in grapes: Shoot shortening, reduced internode length. Critical phenological stage: Pre-bloom or early vegetative growth. Recommended dose (conceptual): 500–1500 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Less persistent than Paclobutrazol; can be used on vigorous varieties.

Category: Growth Retardants. Major use in grapes: Moderate growth control, improved bud fruitfulness. Critical phenological stage: Pre-bloom, early shoot growth. Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–300 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Compatible with most fungicides; do not apply under heat stress.

Category: Growth Retardants. Major use in grapes: Shoot growth inhibition, improved fruit set, reduced pruning. Critical phenological stage: Pre-bloom, early spring. Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–200 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Very short residual – requires multiple applications; safe for most varieties.

Category: Growth Retardants. Major use in grapes: Growth retardation, improved berry colour (older product – restricted in some markets). Critical phenological stage: Pre-bloom to early fruit set. Recommended dose (conceptual): 2000–4000 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Not registered in many regions – check local regulations.

Category: Brassinosteroids. Major use in grapes: Growth promotion, cold/heat tolerance, recovery from stress, improved photosynthesis. Critical phenological stage: Stress periods, Mid-canopy development. Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.1–0.5 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Works in nanogram quantities – precise measuring required. Compatible with most fungicides (except high-pH).

Category: Brassinosteroids. Major use in grapes: Same as above – more potent but less stable. Critical phenological stage: Stress periods. Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.05–0.2 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Very low dose – use certified products; avoid high pH.

Category: Jasmonates. Major use in grapes: Defence induction, improved fruit colour and quality. Critical phenological stage: Pre-harvest (colour enhancement), stress periods. Recommended dose (conceptual): 50–200 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Can cause stomatal closure – apply in evening; do not mix with copper.

Category: Jasmonates. Major use in grapes: Improved berry anthocyanin content, stress tolerance. Critical phenological stage: Veraison (colour development). Recommended dose (conceptual): 50–250 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Volatile – apply quickly; use surfactant.

Category: Salicylates. Major use in grapes: Systemic resistance, heat/cold/drought tolerance, improved fruit firmness. Critical phenological stage: Stress periods, Pre-bloom, Veraison. Recommended dose (conceptual): 50–200 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Compatible with most fungicides (except alkaline); improves antioxidant status.

Category: Strigolactones. Major use in grapes: Root branching, AMF symbiosis enhancement (research tool). Critical phenological stage: Soil application at planting. Recommended dose (conceptual): Not commercialised in grapes. Application method: Soil. Precautions: Mostly research – limited field application.

Category: ABA. Major use in grapes: Berry coloration, ripening synchronisation, stomatal closure (drought tolerance). Critical phenological stage: Veraison (onset of ripening). Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–400 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Highly pH-sensitive (ideal 5.0–6.5). Apply in evening. Do NOT mix with calcium or high-EC fertilisers.

Category: ABA. Major use in grapes: Same as ABA (more active enantiomer). Critical phenological stage: Veraison, Stress (drought). Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–300 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Same as ABA – very light-sensitive; store and apply in cool conditions.

Category: Seaweed. Major use in grapes: Root stimulation, stress tolerance (heat/drought), general vigour, improved fruit quality. Critical phenological stage: 1. Root flush (soil) 2. Pre-bloom (foliar) 3. Post-harvest (foliar). Recommended dose (conceptual): 1–3 L/ha (liquid extract). Application method: Foliar / Soil drench. Precautions: Store in cool, dark place. Compatible with Mancozeb/Captan; avoid mixing with concentrated acids.

Category: Seaweed. Major use in grapes: Cold tolerance, root growth, cytokinin-rich. Critical phenological stage: Dormancy break, Early shoot, Post-stress. Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.5–1.5 L/ha. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Higher auxin content – avoid over-use in hot weather (can cause leaf curling).

Category: Seaweed. Major use in grapes: Stress tolerance, improved yield and quality (rich in nutrients). Critical phenological stage: Vegetative to post-harvest. Recommended dose (conceptual): 1–2 L/ha. Application method: Foliar / Soil. Precautions: Good tank-mix partner with most insecticides; safe on grapes.

Category: Seaweed. Major use in grapes: General stress recovery, soil health. Critical phenological stage: Pre-bloom, Post-stress. Recommended dose (conceptual): 1–2 L/ha. Application method: Soil / Foliar. Precautions: Contains natural growth hormones; compatible with mancozeb.

Category: Seaweed. Major use in grapes: Similar seaweed benefits – vary in cytokinin/auxin content. Critical phenological stage: According to product label. Recommended dose (conceptual): As per label. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Check product pH; most are neutral.

Category: Humics. Major use in grapes: Soil conditioning, nutrient uptake (chelator), root development. Critical phenological stage: Soil: Pre-planting / Root flush. Foliar: Stress periods. Recommended dose (conceptual): 5–10 kg/ha (soil); 1–2 L/ha (foliar liquid). Application method: Soil / Foliar. Precautions: Precipitates in strongly acidic mixes (<pH 5). Do not mix with copper immediately (chelates Cu, reducing fungicide efficacy) – allow 3–5 days gap.

Category: Humics. Major use in grapes: Foliar uptake of nutrients, stress tolerance, phytohormone-like effects. Critical phenological stage: Foliar at stress periods, at fruit set. Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.5–1 L/ha. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Excellent tank-mix partner with Fe/Zn (chelates them). Compatible with most insecticides.

Category: Humics. Major use in grapes: Soil structure improvement (less soluble). Critical phenological stage: Soil application during dormancy. Recommended dose (conceptual): 10–20 kg/ha. Application method: Soil. Precautions: Mostly soil-active – not for foliar.

Category: Amino Acids. Major use in grapes: General stress recovery, pollen viability, improved fruit set, chelation of nutrients. Critical phenological stage: Pre-bloom (pollen), Post-stress, Fruit development. Recommended dose (conceptual): 1–2 L/ha. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Excellent with insecticides (IRAC 4A, 3A). Avoid mixing with strong acids (pH <3).

Category: Amino Acids. Major use in grapes: Precursor to chlorophyll, improved N assimilation, stress recovery. Critical phenological stage: Early growth, Post-stress. Recommended dose (conceptual): 50–100 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Works as signal molecule; compatible with most.

Category: Amino Acids. Major use in grapes: Osmoprotection, stress tolerance (heat/frost), chelator. Critical phenological stage: Stress periods, Pre-bloom. Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–200 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Very stable; can mix with most pesticides.

Category: Amino Acids. Major use in grapes: Osmoprotectant – heat, drought, salt tolerance; stress recovery. Critical phenological stage: Pre-stress (2–3 days before), Post-stress immediately. Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–300 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Pre-stress applications are most effective.

Category: Amino Acids. Major use in grapes: Precursors to ethylene/auxin; stress recovery; pollen tube growth. Critical phenological stage: Pre-bloom, Post-harvest. Recommended dose (conceptual): 50–200 ppm (each). Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Usually applied as a blend – check label for specific ratios.

Category: Botanicals. Major use in grapes: Natural growth promoters, cytokinin sources, antioxidants. Critical phenological stage: Vegetative growth, Stress. Recommended dose (conceptual): 5–10% extract. Application method: Foliar / Soil. Precautions: Variable quality – standardise by using commercial extracts.

topic: Neem / Garlic / Aloe / Licorice / Yucca / Palm
content: Category: Botanicals. Major use in grapes: Induced resistance, stress tolerance, surfactant properties. Critical phenological stage: Stress periods, As adjuvants. Recommended dose (conceptual): As per label. Application method: Foliar / Soil. Precautions: Neem oil (if used) incompatible with sulfur and heat. Yucca acts as surfactant.

Category: Microalgae. Major use in grapes: Plant growth promotion, phytohormone production, nutrient supply. Critical phenological stage: Early growth, Stress recovery. Recommended dose (conceptual): 1–3 L/ha. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Live cultures – do not mix with chemical fungicides (maintain 7-day gap).

Category: Microbial Bacteria. Major use in grapes: Root colonisation, phosphate solubilisation, ISR (induced systemic resistance). Critical phenological stage: Soil: Root flush / Planting. Foliar: Early vegetative. Recommended dose (conceptual): 1–2 kg/ha (CFU based). Application method: Soil drench / Foliar. Precautions: COMPLETELY INCOMPATIBLE with chemical fungicides/bactericides (Copper, Mancozeb, Carbendazim, Streptomycin). Maintain 7–10 day gap.

Category: Microbial Bacteria. Major use in grapes: Similar to Bacillus – P-solubilisation, root health. Critical phenological stage: Root flush, Post-transplant. Recommended dose (conceptual): As per CFU label. Application method: Soil / Foliar. Precautions: Same compatibility issues – keep away from fungicides.

Category: Microbial Bacteria. Major use in grapes: N-fixation (free-living or associative), growth promotion. Critical phenological stage: Soil application pre-planting or at root flush. Recommended dose (conceptual): As per label. Application method: Soil incorporation. Precautions: Do not mix with chemical N-fertilisers in high concentrations (can kill bacteria).

Category: Microbial Fungi. Major use in grapes: Root-zone protection against pathogens, plant growth promotion, soil health. Critical phenological stage: Soil: Root flush, Post-waterlogging Foliar: as bio-protectant. Recommended dose (conceptual): 1–2 kg/ha. Application method: Soil drench / Foliar. Precautions: Incompatible with ALL chemical fungicides. Maintain 7–10 day gap. Add organic matter to enhance colonisation.

Category: Microbial Fungi. Major use in grapes: P & water uptake, root extension, stress tolerance. Critical phenological stage: Pre-planting (nursery) or early root flush. Recommended dose (conceptual): Spores: 100–200/g soil. Application method: Root-dip / Soil incorporation. Precautions: Do NOT fumigate soil before planting AMF. Avoid high-P fertilisers (inhibits colonisation).

Category: Microbial Fungi. Major use in grapes: Plant growth promotion (ISR), nutrient solubilisation. Critical phenological stage: As bio-inoculants. Recommended dose (conceptual): As per label (CFU). Application method: Soil / Foliar. Precautions: Same microbial precautions – separate from chemical fungicides.

Category: Carbohydrates. Major use in grapes: Induced resistance, wound healing, fungistatic action, stress tolerance. Critical phenological stage: Post-stress, Pre-bloom (for disease prevention). Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.1–0.5% (w/v). Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Do NOT mix with strong oxidisers (chlorine, hydrogen peroxide). Can be acidic – check pH.

Category: Carbohydrates. Major use in grapes: Elicitors of plant defence (SAR), stress tolerance. Critical phenological stage: Pre-stress, Post-flowering. Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.1–0.3%. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Typically compatible with most non-alkaline products.

Category: Vitamins. Major use in grapes: Root development, stress resistance, flowering. Critical phenological stage: Early growth, Stress. Recommended dose (conceptual): 10–50 ppm. Application method: Foliar / Soil. Precautions: Often included in commercial blends; very safe, compatible with most.

Category: Vitamins. Major use in grapes: Antioxidant, heat/UV/smoke stress recovery. Critical phenological stage: Post-stress, Pre-harvest. Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–300 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Degrades in light – apply in evening. Compatible with most.

Category: Vitamins. Major use in grapes: Antioxidant, membrane protection. Critical phenological stage: Pre-stress, Post-harvest. Recommended dose (conceptual): 50–150 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Oil-soluble – use emulsifiable formulations; avoid with sulfur.

topic: Citric / Malic / Oxalic / Succinic / Lactic / Acetic
content: Category: Organic Acids. Major use in grapes: pH adjustment, chelation of micronutrients, signalling. Critical phenological stage: As acidifier in tank mixes; as biostimulant in some blends. Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.1–1% (as acidifier). Application method: Tank-mix additive / Foliar. Precautions: Strong acids (citric, oxalic) are incompatible with mancozeb (precipitation). Use for pH correction before adding other products.

Category: Osmoprotectants. Major use in grapes: Osmotic adjustment – heat, drought, salt tolerance. Critical phenological stage: Pre-stress (2–3 days before heat/drought). Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–300 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Excellent for summer heat. Compatible with most insecticides and fungicides.

Category: Osmoprotectants. Major use in grapes: Similar – cellular osmotic balance. Critical phenological stage: Pre-stress, Post-stress. Recommended dose (conceptual): 100–200 ppm (trehalose: 50–100 ppm). Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Proline already listed; sorbitol often used as carrier for boron/calcium.

Category: Silicon. Major use in grapes: Physical barrier (cuticle thickening), drought/heat/salt tolerance, reduced transpiration. Critical phenological stage: Pre-stress, Vegetative growth. Recommended dose (conceptual): 1–3 L/ha (as soluble Si). Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Incompatible with copper (forms insoluble copper silicate – reduces both). Compatible with most others.

Category: Silicon. Major use in grapes: Highly bio-available Si for stress tolerance. Critical phenological stage: Stress periods, Early growth. Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.5–1 L/ha. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Stable at pH 4–7; do not mix with alkaline products.

Category: Silicon. Major use in grapes: Enhanced Si uptake, reduced transpiration, stress tolerance. Critical phenological stage: Pre-stress, Veraison (berry firmness). Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.1–0.5%. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Nano-products are reactive – check compatibility with copper (often incompatible).

Category: Signalling Molecules. Major use in grapes: Stomatal regulation, stress tolerance, ripening. Critical phenological stage: Stress periods, Veraison. Recommended dose (conceptual): 50–200 µM. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Light-sensitive – apply in evening. Experimental; not widely registered.

Category: Signalling Molecules. Major use in grapes: Systemic signalling, stress priming, anti-pathogen. Critical phenological stage: Early growth, Post-stress. Recommended dose (conceptual): 0.1–0.5% (low dose). Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Phytotoxic at >1%. Do not mix with living microbes (kills them).

Category: Signalling Molecules. Major use in grapes: Antioxidant, stress tolerance (heat/cold/drought), ripening. Critical phenological stage: Stress periods, Veraison. Recommended dose (conceptual): 50–150 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: New molecule – check local registration. Compatible with most.

Category: Signalling Molecules. Major use in grapes: Stress tolerance (heat, salinity), improved fruit set. Critical phenological stage: Pre-stress, Pre-bloom. Recommended dose (conceptual): 50–100 ppm. Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Often used in blends; stable, compatible with most except strong oxidisers.

topic: Nano Chitosan / Nano Silicon / Nano Seaweed / Nano Humic / Nano Fulvic
content: Category: Nanobiostimulants. Major use in grapes: Enhanced targeted delivery, higher efficiency. Critical phenological stage: As per base substance. Recommended dose (conceptual): Reduced rates (30–50% of conventional). Application method: Foliar. Precautions: Generally more reactive – jar test essential. Often incompatible with strong electrolytes (calcium, magnesium).

topic: Yeast Extract / Vermiwash / Compost Tea / Biochar Extract / FPE / Effective Microorganisms (EM)
content: Category: Miscellaneous. Major use in grapes: General soil health, phytohormone production, microbial diversity. Critical phenological stage: Soil application at root flush / post-harvest. Recommended dose (conceptual): As per product. Application method: Soil drench / Foliar. Precautions: Variable quality – standardise with commercial products. EM should be separated from chemical fungicides by 7 days.

topic: Tank-mix compatibility - Seaweed Extracts (Ascophyllum, Ecklonia, etc.)
content: Compatibility notes for Seaweed Extracts (Ascophyllum, Ecklonia, etc.) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Caution – pH shift; reduce Cu rate 15%; can chelate Cu slightly. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Avoid – breaks emulsion, causes phytotoxicity at >25°C. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – pH should be 5.5–7.0.

Compatibility notes for Humic / Fulvic Acids (soil/foliar) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Incompatible – chelates Cu, reduces fungicide efficacy. Apply 5 days apart. | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Caution – pH mismatch (humics often alkaline or acidic). | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Incompatible – humics act as surfactants, emulsify oils excessively. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Avoid – if pH drops below 5, humates precipitate.

topic: Tank-mix compatibility - Amino Acids / Protein Hydrolysates (Gly, Pro, Arg, etc.)
content: Compatibility notes for Amino Acids / Protein Hydrolysates (Gly, Pro, Arg, etc.) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Caution – high-pH copper reacts with amino acids (browning). | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Caution – sulfur + amino acids can produce foul odours. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – requires strong agitation to keep mixed. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – amino acids are amphoteric; avoid extreme pH (<3 or >8).

topic: Tank-mix compatibility - Live Microbials (Bacillus, Trichoderma, AMF, Azotobacter, Pseudomonas)
content: Compatibility notes for Live Microbials (Bacillus, Trichoderma, AMF, Azotobacter, Pseudomonas) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Incompatible – kills microbes. | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Incompatible – kills microbes. | Fungicide: Mancozeb / Propineb / Ziram (FRAC M3): Incompatible – kills/stunts growth. | Fungicide: Captan / Chlorothalonil (FRAC M4/M5): Incompatible – kills/stunts growth. | Fungicide: DMI (FRAC 3) / QoI (FRAC 11) / SDHI (FRAC 7): Incompatible – kills/stunts growth. | Fungicide: Carbendazim / Thiophanate (FRAC 1): Incompatible – kills/stunts growth. | Insecticide: OPs (IRAC 1B): Caution – high rates (>label) kill; low rates may be tolerated. | Insecticide: Pyrethroids (IRAC 3A): Caution – generally safe at low rates, but check label. | Insecticide: Neonicotinoids (IRAC 4A / 4C): Caution – can suppress growth; maintain 5–7 day gap. | Insecticide: Spinosad (IRAC 5): Caution – Spinosad is bactericidal? Check label; usually safe. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – oils can suffocate spores. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Avoid – acidic/basic extremes kill spores; pH 6–7 is ideal.

topic: Tank-mix compatibility - PGR: GA₃, 6-BA, CPPU, Kinetin
content: Compatibility notes for PGR: GA₃, 6-BA, CPPU, Kinetin when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Avoid – hydrolysis in alkaline/acidic Cu mixes. | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Avoid – heat + sulfur = phytotoxicity + PGR breakdown. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Avoid – oils reduce absorption via cuticle clogging. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – GA3 degrades in pH >7.0; use buffer.

Compatibility notes for PGR: Ethephon when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Caution – extreme pH mismatch (Ethephon is acidic). | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Incompatible – alkaline reaction causes premature ethylene release. | Fungicide: Mancozeb / Propineb / Ziram (FRAC M3): Caution – hard water affects breakdown; use conditioner. | Fungicide: Captan / Chlorothalonil (FRAC M4/M5): Caution – adjuvants may overload tank. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – oil slows absorption. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Avoid – if pH >7 (releases gas); keep pH 4–6.

Compatibility notes for PGR: ABA (S-ABA) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Caution – high pH degrades ABA. | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Incompatible – ABA counters stress, sulfur adds stress (antagonistic). | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Avoid – ABA is lipophilic; oils alter uptake unpredictably. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – ABA is light-sensitive; apply evening.

topic: Tank-mix compatibility - PGR: Brassinolide / Salicylic Acid / Jasmonates
content: Compatibility notes for PGR: Brassinolide / Salicylic Acid / Jasmonates when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Caution – high pH (copper) degrades some. | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Caution – sulfur can cause stress; avoid combined heat. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – oils reduce penetration. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – pH 5.5–7.0 recommended.

topic: Tank-mix compatibility - Nutrient Chelates (Fe-EDDHA, Zn-EDTA, Mn, B, Ca)
content: Compatibility notes for Nutrient Chelates (Fe-EDDHA, Zn-EDTA, Mn, B, Ca) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Incompatible – Cu displaces chelated metals; precipitation. | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Caution – sulfur + boron can burn. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – can form sticky residues. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – extreme pH chelates break down (e.g., EDTA decomposes <5 and >8).

Compatibility notes for Silicon (Potassium Silicate / OSA) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Incompatible – forms insoluble copper silicate (reduces both). | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – can thicken oil emulsions. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – OSA is stable only at pH 4–7.

Compatibility notes for Osmoprotectants (Glycine Betaine, Trehalose) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Caution – high pH affects stability. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – may need surfactant. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – pH 5.5–7.0.

Compatibility notes for Chitosan / Oligosaccharides when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Caution – chitosan is acidic; can react with Cu. | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Caution – sulfur + chitosan can gel. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – oil + chitosan can form precipitates. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – chitosan dissolves in weak acids (<6); avoid alkaline.

Compatibility notes for Vitamins (C, E, B-complex) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Caution – Vit C is a strong reducing agent; may reduce Cu. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – Vit E is oil-soluble; use emulsified. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Caution – Vit C degrades in alkaline pH.

topic: Tank-mix compatibility - Organic Acids (Citric, Malic, Acetic)
content: Compatibility notes for Organic Acids (Citric, Malic, Acetic) when tank-mixed with common vineyard spray products: Fungicide: Copper (FRAC M1): Caution – acids can dissolve Cu, making it phytotoxic. | Fungicide: Sulfur (FRAC M2): Caution – acid + sulfur can generate H₂S (foul). | Fungicide: Mancozeb / Propineb / Ziram (FRAC M3): Avoid – citric/malic acid precipitate mancozeb (M3). | Fungicide: Captan / Chlorothalonil (FRAC M4/M5): Caution – can degrade Captan in strong acidity. | Fungicide: DMI (FRAC 3) / QoI (FRAC 11) / SDHI (FRAC 7): Caution – very low pH degrades some. | Fungicide: Carbendazim / Thiophanate (FRAC 1): Caution – low pH degrades MBCs. | Spray Oils / EC Formulations: Caution – acid can break oil emulsions. | Alkaline / Acidic Tank-mix Additives: Used as pH correctors – but add before pesticides.
Mix a small sample (1L) of your intended combination in a jar. Shake, wait 30 minutes. If you see sludge, oily film, or excessive foam – do not use in the field.
Most biostimulants (Seaweed, Amino Acids) and PGRs (GA3, ABA) work best at pH 5.5–6.5. Alkaline water (>7.5) destroys them; acidic water (<5.0) precipitates mancozeb and copper.

1. Water (half tank) → 2. Agitation (start) → 3. Liquids / Conditioners → 4. Emulsifiable Concentrates (ECs) / Flowables → 5. Soluble Powders / WGs → Biostimulants / PGRs added LAST (after pH adjustment and pesticides are suspended).
Never mix live microbes (Bacillus, Trichoderma, AMF) with any chemical fungicide or bactericide. Maintain a 7–10 day gap between chemical sprays and microbial applications.
Never mix PGRs (GA3, CPPU) or Seaweed with spray oils when temperature >30°C – oils slow penetration and dramatically increase leaf burn risk.
Log every tank mix: date, product, rate, pH, weather, and observed response. This data is invaluable for troubleshooting and fine-tuning future applications.
